title: Actual bar augmentation from positive-row collapse, with resolution normalization
statement:
Work on the small coherent profinite site in common universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring and $G$ a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Let $N$ be an internal $R$-module with trivial $G$-action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Use ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix compatible nonnegative derived-bar data as in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar, def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. For a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $s:N[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] write
$$C^p=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline G^p],N),\quad D_I^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline G^p],UI^q),\quad V_{I,q}^p=H^q(D_I^{p,\bullet},d_v),$$
with the inhomogeneous action-dependent bar differential $d_h$. The resolution differential $d_v$ commutes with $d_h$, and totalization has finite diagonals and differential $d_h+(-1)^pd_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. All terms with a negative index are zero. Let $a_I:C^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}D_I$ have component in $(p,0)$ induced by $s^0:N\to UI^0$, followed by the $(p,0)$ coprojection; its other source components are zero. Assume, for every such resolution, that
$$H^p(V_{I,q}^\bullet,d_h)=0\quad\text{for every }p\geq0,\ q>0.$$
These are internal module cohomology objects, not the cohomology groups of evaluated section complexes.

Then $a_I$ is a cochain map and a quasi-isomorphism. Its localization is the actual resolution augmentation $Q(C^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline G^p],N[0])$. For every augmentation-preserving equivariant chain map $f:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$, one has the equality of cochain maps
$$\operatorname{Tot}(D_f)\,a_I=a_{I'},$$
and $\operatorname{Tot}(D_f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Such lifts exist between any two resolutions; their localized maps are the canonical changes of resolution, and two lifts induce the same localized map. More explicitly, any equivariant resolution homotopy between lifts induces a total homotopy with its component in bar degree $p$ multiplied by $(-1)^p$. The localized augmentations agree under the canonical identifications between all compatible models. The column-wise quasi-isomorphism hypothesis is a sufficient special case of the displayed row hypothesis.

Finally $C^0=N$, its differential out of degree zero is zero, and under the canonical identification of invariant sections of a trivial action with $N$, the induced degree-zero augmentation is $1_N$. Its square with the invariant-resolution augmentation and the compatible model's total augmentation commutes on degree-zero cohomology. All conclusions retain the specified components of $a_I$; an arbitrary isomorphism of derived objects is not substituted for this morphism.

proof.text: Put $J^{p,0}=C^p$, with horizontal differential $d_C$, and $J^{p,q}=0$ for $q\ne0$. Equivariance of $s^0$ makes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline G^p],s^0)$ commute with every bar face, including the first action face. Also $d_I^0s^0=0$, so these maps give a double-complex morphism $\alpha:J\to D_I$. Under $\operatorname{Tot}J=C^\bullet$, its total map is precisely $a_I$: in degree $n$ the only source summand is $(n,0)$, and its vertical contribution $(-1)^n\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(R[\underline G^n],d_I^0s^0)$ is zero. This proves the cochain-map assertion with the specified components.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), construction of the actual augmentation; compatible action-face specification

proof.text: The computation datum makes $U$ exact, so the underlying resolution has $N=\ker(UI^0\to UI^1)$ via $s^0$. For each $p$, internal $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline G^p],-)$ is a right adjoint by tensor--Hom adjunction, hence preserves this kernel by the right-adjoint limit lemma (the finite parallel-pair index category is small). Since degree $-1$ is zero, it follows that the map induced by $\alpha$ gives $C^p\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{I,0}^p$. Naturality of the kernel comparison with each bar face makes this an isomorphism of horizontal complexes, not merely of the individual objects. This uses left exactness only; positive column cohomology need not vanish.

source.place: Tags 0130 (lemma-ss-double-complex), 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), zero vertical cohomology; internal tensor--Hom adjunction from sites-modules.tex Tag 03EO

proof.text: Apply the first, functorial spectral sequence of double complexes to $\alpha$. For $J$ its second page is $H^p(C^\bullet)$ on $q=0$ and zero elsewhere. For $D_I$ it is $H^p(V_{I,q}^\bullet)$; the hypothesis kills every $q>0$ row, and step 2 identifies the map on the $q=0$ row with an isomorphism. Both totals are first quadrant with exactly the finite-diagonal image filtrations in the cited spectral-sequence theorem. The row-collapse lemma therefore gives edge isomorphisms $E_2^{n,0}\to H^n(\operatorname{Tot}(-))$ for both complexes. Functoriality for $\alpha$ makes their square commute, with bottom map $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}\alpha)=H^n(a_I)$. Its other three maps are isomorphisms, so $H^n(a_I)$ is an isomorphism for every $n\ge0$. Both complexes vanish below zero; thus $a_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The use of this square fixes the morphism, rather than choosing an unrelated abutment isomorphism.

proof.text: For an augmentation-preserving equivariant lift $f:I\to I'$, postcomposition in each internal Hom gives $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(R[\underline G^p],Uf^0)\,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(R[\underline G^p],s^0)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(R[\underline G^p],s'^0)$. After the $(p,0)$ total coprojections these equalities are exactly $\operatorname{Tot}(D_f)a_I=a_{I'}$ as cochain maps. On cohomology, $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}(D_f))=H^n(a_{I'})H^n(a_I)^{-1}$ by step 3, so this total map is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal bar input: functoriality of the specified resolution augmentation; agent argument by the summand equations

proof.text: Apply the existing bar-total naturality lemma in the equivariant abelian category supplied by the compatible data. It supplies lifts of $1_N$ between any two nonnegative injective resolutions, their identity/composition compatibility after localization, and for every equivariant resolution homotopy $h$ the total homotopy $H|_{(p,q)}=(-1)^p\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline G^p],Uh^q)$. In $dH+Hd$ the horizontal terms cancel because their signs are $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$; the vertical terms have sign $(-1)^{2p}=1$. Consequently two lifts give the same localized map; reversing a lift gives its inverse. By the same lemma's derived-unit clause, these are the canonical changes of resolution. Step 4 now makes the localized $a_I$ agree under those changes.

proof.text: The compatible data compute each derived internal Hom on the same underlying injective resolution $UI^\bullet$. The normalized derived comparison is obtained by mapping the specified augmentation and inverting the derived-functor unit on injectives, as in the derived-resolution naturality lemma. Its underived-to-derived map in bar degree $p$ is therefore represented by postcomposition with $s^0$, not by a freely chosen isomorphism. Taking the finite-diagonal total gives exactly $Q(a_I)$ as the actual resolution augmentation into $\operatorname{Tot}_{p\ge0}R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[\underline G^p],N[0])$. Normalized comparisons assemble for the whole bar diagram by that lemma; the compatible model isomorphisms are fixed on summands by their evaluations and augmentations. Together with step 5, this proves agreement for all compatible models.

source.place: Tags 013P and 013S, normalized injective-resolution computation; agent internal-bar model specialization

proof.text: If the column augmentations $C^p[0]\to D_I^{p,\bullet}$ are quasi-isomorphisms, then $V_{I,q}^p=0$ for every $p\ge0,q>0$. Each positive horizontal cohomology row is consequently the zero complex, so the displayed row hypothesis follows. Thus column-wise quasi-isomorphism is the asserted sufficient special case, without imposing it on steps 1--6.

Evaluation on $G^0=*$ identifies $C^0=N$; the two degree-zero faces are $n\mapsto(g\mapsto g n)$ and $n\mapsto(g\mapsto n)$, so $d_C^0=0$ for the trivial action and $H^0(C)=N$. The kernel of the total differential out of $D_I^{0,0}=UI^0$ consists of sections with $d_Ix=0$ and $gx=x$ after every profinite base change. Via the kernel inclusion $s^0$ it is exactly $N$, all of whose sections are fixed. Hence $H^0(a_I)$ is $1_N$ under this specified identification. Write $u:N[0]\to\Gamma_G(I^\bullet)$ for the invariant-resolution augmentation, $b_I:\Gamma_G(I^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}D_I$ for the model augmentation, and $c:N[0]\to C^\bullet$ for the identity in degree zero. Then $b_Iu=a_Ic$: in degree zero both are $s^0$ followed by the $(0,0)$ coprojection, and all other source terms are zero. The same kernel computation identifies $H^0(u)$ with $1_N$. Applying $H^0$ gives the required commuting square; normalization of the compatible model by $b_I$ preserves it.
